one_line.text: American writer and speaker who translates research on habits, decision-making and continuous improvement into practical systems.

biography.text: Clear began writing at JamesClear.com in 2012 and built a large audience through articles and his 3-2-1 newsletter. Atomic Habits, published in 2018, was his first book. He previously played college baseball at Denison University and describes rebuilding routines after a serious high-school injury as part of the book's origin story.

background.text: His background is independent writing, synthesis, speaking and personal experimentation rather than academic psychology. He explicitly describes his work as finding existing ideas across fields and explaining them in an actionable form.

expertise.text: Clear has strong practical expertise in communicating behaviour-change ideas, designing simple frameworks and turning them into tools. He is not a habit researcher or clinician, so scientific and treatment claims need support from the underlying research rather than his authority.

perspective_and_limits.text: He favours small repeatable actions, environmental design and personal agency. That lens makes change feel workable and reduces reliance on motivation, but it can understate illness, disability, poverty, care duties, workplace power and other conditions that cannot be redesigned by one person.
